newsitem.title: Indonesia: Indonesia launches $2.5 bln rail, road project.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia launches $2.5 bln rail, road project.

text.p: An Indonesian conglomerate controlled by President Suharto's daughter on Monday launched a $2.5 billion project to build a three-tier rail and road project in a bid to ease chronic traffic jams in the capital, Jakarta.

PT Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada, owned by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana, said it would form a joint venture with state-owned toll-road operator PT Jasa Marga and railway company Perumka to build the project.
The joint venture is 80 percent owned by Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada and 10 percent each by Jasa Marga and Perumka.
"God willing, this project will help ease traffic jams in this beloved city," Rukmana said in a speech at a ceremony marking the setting up of the new company, PT Citra Moda Margakencana Persada.

"The number of people and vehicles has been growing rapidly, so we need a transportation system which can help ease traffic jams," said Rukmana, who also controls toll road operator PT Citra Marga Nursaphala Persada.

The elevated three-tier thoroughfare, which will connect the Blok M shopping area in south Jakarta to the central business district and to the Kota old town area in northern Jakarta, will consist of a 23.65 km (14.78 mile) toll road, a 22 km (13.75 mile) railway line and a public road.
Construction is to start in December and the project will be completed in 2001, officials involved in the project have said. Funding will be from a consortium of domestic and foreign banks.

The streets of Jakarta, a city of 10 million people and 1.5 million vehicles, are often clogged at rush-hour, with lines of vehicles immobile on the few arterial roads running from office areas in the north to suburban residential areas in the south.
The city's current railway system only touches the periphery of the business district and most commuters use buses or their own cars.

Bambang Soeroso, chief executive of the joint venture, told reporters a railway track would be built on the second level of the thoroughfare and would have 22 stations linked by light-rail commuter trains.
Soeroso, who is also the project's coordinator, said 120,000 people an hour were expected to use the trains in a single direction once the project was completed.
He said the toll road, on the top level and to be operated by Jasa Marga, would accommodate 101,000 cars a day, each being charged 6,500 rupiah ($2.70) a trip.
Soeroso also said that funding, which would involve domestic and foreign banks, was still being worked out.
"This is a big project and members of the consortium should also be big. Forty percent of the funding will come from domestic banks and 60 percent from foreign banks," he said.
Soeroso said the new company had invited foreign investors to take part. "We are still finalising the details," he said.

Soeroso was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying in February that a syndicate of 61 banks, including institutions from Hong Kong, Canada and Singapore as well as 51 domestic banks, would provide loans for the project.
